summary: Outlines the transition of NIC services. It is informational and describes the plan for moving how those services are provided.

plainLanguage.summary: The place that kept the Internet's information was changing who ran it. This explains the move.

questions: what is the network information center
subtitle: The Network Information Center moved to a new organization in October 1991.

tldr.problem: The Network Information Center, which managed domain names and network registrations for the Internet, was operated by SRI International and needed to transition to a new organization.
tldr.mechanism: Government Systems Inc. took over NIC operations on October 1, 1991, with a planned handoff from SRI in September. Most services remained the same, though the operating system changed from TOPS20 to SunOS.
tldr.outcome: The transition was completed with minimal disruption, moving NIC to Virginia and establishing new contact information and procedures.

today: RFC 1261 is a historical informational document describing infrastructure changes in 1991. The NIC function evolved into IANA (Internet Assigned Numbers Authority) and domain registration services are now handled by many accredited registrars worldwide.

sections.title: The NIC Transition
sections.content:
The Network Information Center (NIC) maintained critical information for the Internet: network numbers, domain name registrations, RFC archives, and a Help Desk for users. This document announces the formal transition of NIC services from SRI International in Menlo Park, California, to Government Systems Inc. in Chantilly, Virginia, effective October 1, 1991.

SRI would continue providing all services and responding to user requests through September 30, 1991, ensuring time for the transfer.
sections.plainLanguage: The office keeping Internet records moved to a new location. For a month, both places helped users, then only the new place stayed open.

sections.title: New Contact Information and Systems
sections.content:
The new NIC at Government Systems Inc. operated from Chantilly, Virginia. The Help Desk telephone numbers became 1-800-365-DNIC (1-800-365-3642) and 1-703-802-4535, with hours from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM Eastern Time. The fax number was 1-703-802-8376.

The new NIC host was a Sun 470 SPARCserver running SunOS 4.1, replacing the previous TOPS20 operating system. The network address remained 192.112.36.5 (NIC.DDN.MIL), and the root domain server was 192.112.36.4 (NS.NIC.DDN.MIL). Most on-line services appeared the same to users, with minor differences due to the operating system change.
sections.plainLanguage: The new office had different phone numbers and computers, but the services stayed mostly the same.

sections.title: Transition Timeline and Database Freeze
sections.content:
From September 26 to September 30, 1991, the ID database (WHOIS) was frozen and registration actions were suspended to allow the master database to be transferred to GSI. Starting September 26, all U.S. mail and fax requests were directed to the new GSI address and fax number. Electronic mail requests continued to go to the HOSTMASTER and REGISTRAR mailboxes at NIC.DDN.MIL, with SRI redirecting them to GSI as appropriate.

Registration activities resumed on October 1, 1991, when the new NIC officially took over operations.
sections.plainLanguage: During the move, the database could not change to avoid losing information. Once moved, everything went back to normal.
